label: 802.1x Wired
description: IEEE 802.1X wired authentication provides port-based network access control for wired Ethernet connections. The Wired AutoConfig service (dot3svc) enforces authentication using EAP methods such as EAP-TLS (certificate-based) or PEAP-MSCHAPv2 (username/password). Clients authenticate to a RADIUS server (typically Microsoft NPS) which authorizes network access and can assign VLANs. This scenario covers troubleshooting authentication failures, certificate issues, switch port configuration, NPS policy matching, and wired profile deployment via Group Policy.

l1: What Windows version is the authenticating client running? (Get-ComputerInfo | Select OsName,OsVersion,WindowsVersion)
What is the exact symptom — switchport stuck in unauthorized state (no network), placed in guest/restricted VLAN, wrong VLAN assigned, or intermittent drops?
Is this affecting all ports on the switch, a specific switch, or only specific ports?
What switch vendor, model, and firmware/IOS version is the authenticating switch?
Is the switch configured for 802.1x with NPS (Microsoft RADIUS) as the authentication server?
What host mode is configured on the switch port — single-host, multi-host, multi-auth, or multi-domain (data + voice)?
Is the Wired AutoConfig service (dot3svc) running and set to Automatic on the Windows client? (Get-Service dot3svc | Select Name,Status,StartType,DisplayName)
Is the client using EAP-TLS (machine or user certificate), PEAP-MSCHAPv2 (username/password), or PEAP-TLS?
When did this start — switch firmware update, certificate renewal, GPO change, NPS configuration change, or new client machine?
Is the Ethernet adapter connected and showing as 'Up'? (Get-NetAdapter | Where Status -eq 'Up' | Select Name,InterfaceDescription,Status)
l2: What EAP method is configured in the Wired Network (IEEE 802.3) Group Policy — EAP-TLS, PEAP-MSCHAPv2, or a combined method?
Is the Wired Network IEEE 802.3 GPO applied to the affected machine? (gpresult /r | findstr -i '802.3\|wired\|IEEE')

Is the client machine certificate issued by the correct internal CA, not expired, and present in the LocalMachine\My certificate store? (Get-ChildItem -Path Cert:\LocalMachine\My | Select Subject,Issuer,NotBefore,NotAfter,EnhancedKeyUsageList)
Is the NPS Network Policy condition NAS-Port-Type set to Ethernet (value 15) for this wired policy?
Is the switch sending NAS-Port-Type = 15 (Ethernet) in the RADIUS Access-Request — or a different value based on switch vendor configuration?
Is MAC Authentication Bypass (MAB) configured as a fallback for printers, IP phones, or non-802.1x-capable devices?
Is the client machine account a member of the AD security group required by the NPS Network Policy conditions? (Get-ADComputer <computername> -Properties MemberOf | Select MemberOf)
What Authentication Order is configured on the switch — dot1x first, then MAB, or MAB first? What are the timeouts?
Is the wired AutoConfig profile deployed as a Computer Configuration GPO (recommended) or User Configuration GPO?
What is the NPS server version and is it configured with the correct RADIUS clients (switches)? (Get-Service IAS | Select Name,Status; netsh nps show client)

Are there any recent 802.1x-related events in the Wired-AutoConfig/Operational log? (Get-WinEvent -LogName Microsoft-Windows-Wired-AutoConfig/Operational -MaxEvents 10 | Format-List TimeCreated,Id,LevelDisplayName,Message)
Is the switch configured with the correct RADIUS shared secret matching the NPS configuration?

l1: Run 'Get-Service dot3svc | Select Name,Status,StartType,DisplayName' — is Wired AutoConfig running and set to Automatic?
Run 'gpresult /r | findstr -i "802.3\|wired\|IEEE"' — is the Wired Network GPO listed in Applied GPOs?

Check Security event log for Event ID 5632 (802.1x authentication request sent) and 5633 (802.1x authentication failed) — share the error code from Event 5633. (Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=5632 or EventID=5633)]]" -MaxEvents 20 | Format-List TimeCreated,Id,Message)
On the switch: 'show dot1x interface <interface>' — what is the current authentication state (Authorized/Unauthorized)?
On the switch: 'show authentication sessions interface <interface>' — share the Method, Username, VLAN, and Session-state.
Run 'netsh lan show profiles' — is the correct 802.1x wired profile configured on the client?
Run 'netsh lan show interfaces' — confirm the wired interface is present and in a connected state.

On the NPS server: check Security log for Event 6273 with the Calling-Station-Id matching this client's MAC address. (Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=6273)]]" -MaxEvents 30 | Format-List TimeCreated,Message)
Verify the Ethernet adapter is connected: 'Get-NetAdapter | Where Status -eq 'Up' | Select Name,InterfaceDescription,MacAddress,LinkSpeed'
Check for recent Wired-AutoConfig events: 'Get-WinEvent -LogName Microsoft-Windows-Wired-AutoConfig/Operational -MaxEvents 20 | Format-Table TimeCreated,Id,LevelDisplayName -AutoSize'
l2: Run 'netsh lan show profile name="<profile>"' — share full EAP type, authentication mode, and certificate selection criteria. (netsh lan show profile name="<profile>" | Select-String -Pattern 'EAP','OneX','Authentication')

On NPS: filter Security log Event 6273 — note Reason-Code (field 9), Client-IP (NAS IP), Calling-Station-Id (client MAC), and Filter-Id. Parse the Reason Code: 1=Internal error, 2=Access denied, 3=Account disabled, 22=Account not found, 23=Wrong password, 48=No policy matched, 65=EAP failure.

Run 'Get-ChildItem -Path Cert:\LocalMachine\My | Select Subject,Issuer,NotBefore,NotAfter,Thumbprint,EnhancedKeyUsageList | Format-List' — confirm the machine certificate subject, thumbprint, expiry, and enhanced key usage (must include Client Authentication OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.2).
Capture 802.1x wired trace: 'netsh trace start capture=yes provider=Microsoft-Windows-Wired-AutoConfig level=5 tracefile=C:\wired_8021x.etl' — reproduce — stop with 'netsh trace stop'.

On the switch (during maintenance): enable 'debug dot1x' and 'debug radius authentication' — capture the full EAP exchange messages. For Cisco: 'debug dot1x all', 'debug radius authentication'. For other vendors, consult vendor-specific debug commands.

Run 'Get-WinEvent -LogName Microsoft-Windows-Wired-AutoConfig/Operational | Sort TimeCreated -Descending | Select -First 50 | Format-List TimeCreated,Id,LevelDisplayName,Message' — analyze for EAP method negotiation failures.
Verify RADIUS shared secret on NPS for this switch: 'netsh nps show client name="<switch name>"' — confirm the shared secret matches the switch configuration.

Run 'gpresult /h C:\gpo_report.html' — open and inspect Computer Configuration > Applied GPOs for the Wired Network (IEEE 802.3) policy name. Check for WMI filters or security filtering that might block application.
Run 'certutil -store -enterprise NTAuthCertificates' — is the issuing CA in the NTAuth store (required for Kerberos-based EAP-TLS)?
Check certificate chain and revocation: 'certutil -verify -urlfetch <certificate_thumbprint>' — confirms certificate chain is valid and CRL/OCSP is reachable.

Verify EAP-TLS certificate has correct properties: 'Get-ChildItem -Path Cert:\LocalMachine\My | Where {$_.EnhancedKeyUsageList -like "*Client Authentication*"} | Select Subject,Issuer,HasPrivateKey,NotAfter'
Check for root CA trust: 'Get-ChildItem -Path Cert:\LocalMachine\Root | Where Issuer -like "*<your CA>*"' — confirm root CA is in trusted store.
Test RADIUS connectivity from switch to NPS: 'test aaa group radius <username> <password> new-code' (Cisco) or vendor-specific equivalent.
Check NPS event log for authentication failures: 'Get-WinEvent -LogName Microsoft-Windows-NPS/Operational -MaxEvents 30 | Format-Table TimeCreated,Id,LevelDisplayName -AutoSize'
Verify switch port authentication configuration: 'show running-config interface <interface> | include authentication,dot1x' — confirm 802.1x is enabled and configured correctly.

l1: Start and set Wired AutoConfig to Automatic: 'Set-Service dot3svc -StartupType Automatic; Start-Service dot3svc; Get-Service dot3svc'
Force GPO refresh: 'gpupdate /force /target:computer' — verify with 'netsh lan show profiles' and 'gpresult /r | findstr -i 802.3'

Verify machine certificate is present, not expired, and from the correct CA: 'Get-ChildItem -Path Cert:\LocalMachine\My | Where {$_.Subject -like "*<machine FQDN>*"} | Select Subject,Issuer,NotBefore,NotAfter,EnhancedKeyUsageList'

Bounce the switch port during a maintenance window: 'shutdown' then 'no shutdown' — forces a new authentication cycle. Alternatively, disable/enable the Ethernet adapter on the client: 'Disable-NetAdapter -Name "<adapter>"; Enable-NetAdapter -Name "<adapter>"'
Confirm NPS Network Policy NAS-Port-Type = 15 (Ethernet) matches what the switch sends. Check NPS Network Policy conditions and switch RADIUS configuration.
For PEAP-MSCHAPv2: verify user password is not expired — 'Get-ADUser <user> -Properties PasswordExpired,PasswordLastSet | Select PasswordExpired,PasswordLastSet'
Verify the Ethernet adapter is enabled and connected: 'Enable-NetAdapter -Name "<adapter>"; Get-NetAdapter | Where Status -eq 'Up'
Check for network profile conflicts: 'netsh lan delete profile name="<profile>"' then 'gpupdate /force' to redeploy clean profile.
l2: EAP-TLS Certificate Issues: Confirm cert has SAN or CN matching the machine FQDN, Client Authentication EKU (1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.2), private key is available (HasPrivateKey = $true), and is in LocalMachine\My. Run: 'Get-ChildItem -Path Cert:\LocalMachine\My | Where {$_.Subject -like "*<FQDN>*"} | Select Subject,Issuer,HasPrivateKey,NotAfter,EnhancedKeyUsageList,SubjectAlternativeNames'

EAP-TLS Chain Validation: Verify the issuing CA certificate chain is complete and trusted. Run: 'certutil -verify -urlfetch <thumbprint>' to check CRL/OCSP reachability. Ensure root CA is in Cert:\LocalMachine\Root store.

EAP-TLS NTAuth Store: For Kerberos-based EAP-TLS, the issuing CA must be in the NTAuthCertificates store. Run: 'certutil -store -enterprise NTAuthCertificates' and verify your CA is listed. Add if missing: 'certutil -addstore -enterprise NTAuthCertificates <CA cert file>'

Machine Account Group Membership: For machine account not in required AD group: 'Add-ADGroupMember -Identity "<group>" -Members "<computer>$"' — machine must reboot to refresh its Kerberos PAC. Verify with: 'Get-ADComputer <computername> -Properties MemberOf | Select MemberOf'

MAB Fallback Failure: On the switch, verify 'authentication event no-response action authorize vlan <restricted VLAN>' is configured and the MAC is in the RADIUS client database. Check switch logs for MAB authentication attempts. For Cisco: 'show authentication sessions interface <int> details'

Wired Profile GPO Application Issues: Check GPRESULT — is policy in Denied GPOs? Check WMI filter or security filtering on the GPO object in GPMC. Run: 'gpresult /h C:\gpo_report.html' and inspect the report. Check GPO status in GPMC under Computer Configuration > Policies > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Wired Network (IEEE 802.3) Policies.

VLAN Assignment Issues: Verify NPS Network Policy RADIUS attributes — Tunnel-Type (value 13 = VLAN), Tunnel-Medium-Type (value 6 = 802), Tunnel-Pvt-Group-ID (VLAN ID as a string, not integer). In NPS console: Policy Settings > Network Policy > Settings > RADIUS Attributes > Standard. Ensure VLAN ID is formatted as string (e.g., "10" not 10).

EAP-TLS Certificate Template Issues: Verify the certificate was issued from the correct template with required extensions. Run: 'certutil -store My <thumbprint>' and check Template property. Ensure template has Client Authentication EKU and correct certificate purpose.

PEAP-MSCHAPv2 Server Certificate Validation: On the client, verify the NPS/RADIUS server certificate is trusted. Check Cert:\LocalMachine\Root for the issuing CA. PEAP requires server certificate validation. Disable temporarily for testing (not recommended for production): In wired profile properties, uncheck 'Validate server certificate'.

Wired AutoConfig Service Dependencies: Check if service has dependency issues. Run: 'Get-Service dot3svc | Select Name,Status,StartType,ServicesDependedOn'. Ensure required services (RPC, etc.) are running.

Switch Port Host Mode Issues: For multi-host/multi-auth issues, verify the switch port host mode matches your deployment. For single-host mode, only one device can authenticate. For multi-domain, ensure CDP/LLDP is detecting voice devices correctly. Run: 'show cdp neighbors interface <int>' or 'show lldp neighbors interface <int>'

NPS Policy Matching Failures: Use NPS logging to identify why no policy matched. Enable NPS accounting/logging: 'netsh nps set config logging accountinglog=enabled' and 'netsh nps set config configperiod=60'. Check C:\Windows\System32\LogFiles\ for log files.

RADIUS Shared Secret Mismatch: If authentication fails with 'Shared secret incorrect' error, reconfigure the shared secret on both NPS and switch. On NPS: RADIUS Clients > Properties > Shared Secret. On switch: radius-server host <IP> key <secret>. Ensure no trailing spaces or special characters.

Multi-Domain Mode (Voice + Data): For multi-domain mode issues on phone + PC same port, confirm switch detects phone via CDP/LLDP — 'show cdp neighbors interface <int>' — and assigns it to the voice VLAN. Verify voice VLAN configuration: 'switchport voice vlan <vlan>'. Check authentication order: dot1x before mab for data, mab for voice.

Analyze Wired AutoConfig ETL Trace: Use Event Viewer or 'tracerpt C:\wired_8021x.etl -o C:\wired_report.evtx -of EVTX' — look for EAP method negotiation failure, TLS Alert codes, or RADIUS timeout events. Key events to look for: EAP identity request/response, TLS handshake stages, certificate validation, and RADIUS Access-Challenge/Accept/Reject messages.

Switch Authentication Timer Issues: If authentication times out, adjust switch timers. For Cisco: 'dot1x timeout tx-period <seconds>', 'dot1x timeout supp-timeout <seconds>', 'dot1x timeout max-req <count>'. Ensure timers are compatible with client retransmission settings.

Certificate Revocation Checking: If certificate validation fails due to CRL/OCSP issues, check network connectivity to CRL distribution points. Run: 'certutil -verify -urlfetch <thumbprint>' to test. If needed, disable CRL checking temporarily for testing (not production): in registry, set HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Internet Settings\CertificateRevocation = 0.

EAP Method Configuration Mismatch: Ensure the EAP method configured in the wired profile matches the NPS network policy. For EAP-TLS, both client and server must be configured for TLS. For PEAP, verify inner method (MSCHAPv2) matches on both ends. Check profile: 'netsh lan show profile name="<profile>"'

Network Policy Priority Conflicts: In NPS, verify network policies are ordered correctly. Policies are processed top-to-bottom; first matching policy is applied. Ensure your wired 802.1x policy is positioned above catch-all policies. Check policy conditions and ensure they don't overlap incorrectly.

DHCP Issues Post-Authentication: If authentication succeeds but no IP is obtained, check DHCP scope for the assigned VLAN. Verify switch port is in correct VLAN: 'show interface <int> switchport'. Test with static IP to isolate DHCP vs authentication issues.

l1: Export wired network profiles: 'netsh lan show profiles > C:\wired_8021x_profiles.txt'
Export wired interface status: 'netsh lan show interfaces > C:\wired_interfaces.txt'
Export Security event log (client): 'wevtutil epl Security C:\Security_Events_Client.evtx'
Generate GPO report: 'gpresult /h C:\gpo_report.html'
Collect Wired AutoConfig service status: 'Get-Service dot3svc | Select Name,Status,StartType,DisplayName,ServicesDependedOn | Out-File C:\dot3svc_status.txt'
Export Wired-AutoConfig Operational log: 'wevtutil epl Microsoft-Windows-Wired-AutoConfig/Operational C:\Wired_AutoConfig_Operational.evtx'
Collect network adapter configuration: 'Get-NetAdapter | Where Status -eq 'Up' | Select Name,InterfaceDescription,MacAddress,LinkSpeed,Status | Format-List | Out-File C:\net_adapter_config.txt'
Export recent 802.1x security events: 'Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=5632 or EventID=5633)]]" -MaxEvents 50 | Export-Clixml C:\8021x_security_events.xml'
l2: Capture wired 802.1x trace: 'netsh trace start capture=yes provider=Microsoft-Windows-Wired-AutoConfig level=5 tracefile=C:\wired_8021x_trace.etl' — reproduce issue — stop with 'netsh trace stop'
Export detailed wired profile configuration: 'netsh lan show profile name="<profile>" > C:\wired_profile_detailed.txt'

Export machine certificate store: 'Get-ChildItem -Path Cert:\LocalMachine\My | Select Subject,Issuer,NotBefore,NotAfter,Thumbprint,EnhancedKeyUsageList,HasPrivateKey | Format-List | Out-File C:\machine_cert_store.txt'
Export root CA certificates: 'Get-ChildItem -Path Cert:\LocalMachine\Root | Select Subject,Issuer,NotBefore,NotAfter | Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-File C:\root_ca_store.txt'
Export NTAuthCertificates store: 'certutil -store -enterprise NTAuthCertificates > C:\ntauth_certs.txt'

Collect NPS configurations: 'netsh nps show np > C:
ps_network_policies.txt'; 'netsh nps show crp > C:
ps_connection_request_policies.txt'; 'netsh nps show client > C:
ps_radius_clients.txt'
Export NPS event log: 'wevtutil epl Microsoft-Windows-NPS/Operational C:\NPS_Operational.evtx'
Collect switch outputs: 'show dot1x all', 'show authentication sessions', 'show radius statistics', 'show running-config interface <interface>', 'show mac address-table interface <interface>'
Export certificate chain with validation: 'certutil -verify -urlfetch <thumbprint> > C:\cert_chain_validation.txt'
Collect detailed Wired-AutoConfig events: 'Get-WinEvent -LogName Microsoft-Windows-Wired-AutoConfig/Operational -MaxEvents 100 | Export-Clixml C:\wired_events_detailed.xml'
Collect system information: 'Get-ComputerInfo | Select OsName,OsVersion,WindowsVersion,OsHardwareAbstractionLayer | Out-File C:\system_info.txt'
Export IP configuration: 'ipconfig /all > C:\ipconfig_all.txt'
Collect AD computer group membership: 'Get-ADComputer <computername> -Properties MemberOf,LastLogonDate | Select MemberOf,LastLogonDate | Out-File C:\ad_computer_info.txt'
Export registry settings for Wired AutoConfig: 'reg export HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\dot3svc C:\dot3svc_registry.reg'
Collect RADIUS authentication events from NPS: 'Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=6273)]]" -MaxEvents 100 | Export-Clixml C:\nps_auth_events.xml'

TSS full data collection: '.\TSS.ps1 -Scenario NET_802Dot1x' — run on the affected client, reproduce the authentication failure, stop when prompted. This collects comprehensive networking and authentication data.

Export network adapter binding information: 'Get-NetAdapterBinding | Where InterfaceAlias -like "*Ethernet*" | Select InterfaceAlias,ComponentID,Enabled | Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-File C:\adapter_bindings.txt'
Collect DHCP client events: 'Get-WinEvent -LogName Microsoft-Windows-DHCP-Client/Operational -MaxEvents 50 | Export-Clixml C:\dhcp_events.xml'

port_unauthorized.title: Switchport stuck in unauthorized state — no network
port_unauthorized.description: Troubleshoots 802.1x wired authentication failures where the switch port remains in an unauthorized state, blocking all network access. This playbook covers Wired AutoConfig service issues, GPO profile deployment, certificate problems, and NPS authentication failures.

steps.action: Get-Service dot3svc | Select Name,Status,StartType,DisplayName
steps.expect: Status: Running, StartType: Automatic — service must be running for 802.1x to function

steps.action: On switch: show dot1x interface <port>
steps.expect: Auth state: Unauthorized — confirms 802.1x is blocking the port

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=5632 or EventID=5633)]]" -MaxEvents 10 | Format-List TimeCreated,Id,Message
steps.expect: Event 5633 = 802.1x auth failed — note the error code for root cause analysis

steps.action: Get-NetAdapter | Where Status -eq 'Up' | Select Name,Status
steps.expect: Ethernet adapter is connected and showing 'Up' status

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=6273)]]" -MaxEvents 10 on NPS server | Format-List TimeCreated,Message
steps.expect: Reason Code identifies root cause — 22=account not found, 23=wrong password, 48=no policy matched, 65=EAP failure

steps.action: netsh lan show profiles
steps.expect: Correct 802.1x wired profile present on client

steps.action: gpresult /r | findstr -i '802.3\|wired\|IEEE'
steps.expect: Wired Network IEEE 802.3 GPO listed in Applied GPOs

steps.action: Get-ChildItem -Path Cert:\LocalMachine\My | Where {$_.EnhancedKeyUsageList -like "*Client Authentication*"} | Select Subject,NotAfter
steps.expect: Valid machine certificate with Client Authentication EKU exists and is not expired

steps.action: Set-Service dot3svc -StartupType Automatic; Start-Service dot3svc; Get-Service dot3svc
steps.expect: Wired AutoConfig service running and set to Automatic

steps.action: gpupdate /force /target:computer
steps.expect: Wired 802.1x profile refreshed from GPO — verify with netsh lan show profiles

steps.action: On switch: shutdown then no shutdown on the port
steps.expect: Forces new authentication cycle after client-side fix

steps.action: If certificate issue: Ensure certificate has private key and correct EKU — re-enroll if needed
steps.expect: Valid certificate present with required properties

steps.action: On switch: show authentication sessions interface <port>
steps.expect: Auth state: Authorized, correct VLAN assigned

steps.action: ipconfig /all on client
steps.expect: Valid IP address received from correct VLAN scope

steps.action: Test network connectivity: ping <gateway IP>
steps.expect: Successful ping to default gateway confirms network access

vlan_not_assigned.title: Wrong VLAN assigned after wired 802.1x authentication
vlan_not_assigned.description: Addresses scenarios where 802.1x authentication succeeds but the client is placed in an incorrect VLAN. This typically involves NPS RADIUS attribute configuration issues, specifically Tunnel-Type, Tunnel-Medium-Type, and Tunnel-Pvt-Group-ID values.

steps.action: On switch: show authentication sessions interface <port>
steps.expect: Auth succeeds but VLAN shown is wrong

steps.action: ipconfig /all on client
steps.expect: IP is in wrong subnet — confirms VLAN assignment issue not auth issue

steps.action: On switch: show interface <port> switchport
steps.expect: Verify the port is actually in the VLAN shown by authentication sessions

steps.action: netsh nps show np — check RADIUS attributes on matching Network Policy
steps.expect: Tunnel-Type=13, Tunnel-Medium-Type=6, Tunnel-Pvt-Group-ID=<VLAN ID as string>

steps.action: On switch: show running-config interface <port>
steps.expect: Confirm switchport is configured to accept RADIUS-assigned VLAN (e.g., 'authentication port-control auto', 'dot1x pae authenticator')

steps.action: Check NPS event log for VLAN assignment: Get-WinEvent -LogName Microsoft-Windows-NPS/Operational -MaxEvents 20
steps.expect: Events show which Network Policy matched and what RADIUS attributes were sent

steps.action: In NPS console: correct Tunnel-Pvt-Group-ID to the correct VLAN ID as a string value
steps.expect: VLAN ID corrected — note it must be a string not integer type (e.g., "10" not 10)

steps.action: Verify Tunnel-Type is set to 13 (VLAN) and Tunnel-Medium-Type is set to 6 (802)
steps.expect: Both attributes correctly configured in NPS Network Policy

steps.action: If using vendor-specific attributes, ensure switch supports the VSA format used
steps.expect: VSA configuration matches switch requirements

steps.action: Re-authenticate: on switch shutdown then no shutdown on port
steps.expect: Client re-authenticates and receives correct VLAN

steps.action: ipconfig /all on client
steps.expect: IP address in correct VLAN subnet

steps.action: On switch: show authentication sessions interface <port>
steps.expect: Shows correct VLAN ID in session information

eaptls_cert_failure.title: EAP-TLS certificate authentication failure
eaptls_cert_failure.description: Troubleshoots EAP-TLS authentication failures related to client certificate issues. Covers certificate validity, chain trust, EKU requirements, private key availability, and NTAuth store configuration for Kerberos-based authentication.

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=5633)]]" -MaxEvents 5 | Format-List Message
steps.expect: Event 5633 shows EAP-TLS specific error code (often related to certificate issues)

steps.action: Get-ChildItem -Path Cert:\LocalMachine\My | Where {$_.Subject -like "*<machine FQDN>*"} | Select Subject,NotAfter,HasPrivateKey
steps.expect: Certificate exists, is not expired, and has private key

steps.action: Get-ChildItem -Path Cert:\LocalMachine\My | Where {$_.Subject -like "*<machine FQDN>*"} | Select EnhancedKeyUsageList
steps.expect: Enhanced Key Usage includes Client Authentication (1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.2)

steps.action: certutil -verify -urlfetch <thumbprint>
steps.expect: Certificate chain validates successfully, CRL/OCSP is reachable

steps.action: certutil -store -enterprise NTAuthCertificates
steps.expect: Issuing CA is listed in NTAuthCertificates store (required for Kerberos EAP-TLS)

steps.action: Get-ChildItem -Path Cert:\LocalMachine\Root | Where Issuer -like "*<issuing CA>*"
steps.expect: Root CA certificate is present in trusted root store

steps.action: Get-ChildItem -Path Cert:\LocalMachine\My | Where {$_.Subject -like "*<machine FQDN>*"} | Select SubjectAlternativeNames
steps.expect: SAN contains machine FQDN or CN matches FQDN

steps.action: If certificate expired: Request new certificate from certificate template
steps.expect: New certificate issued with valid dates

steps.action: If missing private key: Re-enroll for certificate using certmgr.msc or auto-enrollment
steps.expect: Certificate now has HasPrivateKey = $true

steps.action: If CA not in NTAuth: certutil -addstore -enterprise NTAuthCertificates <CA cert file>
steps.expect: CA added to NTAuthCertificates store

steps.action: If chain validation fails: Ensure intermediate CAs are in appropriate certificate stores
steps.expect: Complete certificate chain from leaf to root is present

steps.action: Re-authenticate: disable/enable Ethernet adapter or bounce switch port
steps.expect: EAP-TLS authentication succeeds

steps.action: On switch: show authentication sessions interface <port>
steps.expect: Auth state: Authorized, method shows EAP-TLS

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=5632)]]" -MaxEvents 5
steps.expect: Event 5632 indicates successful 802.1x authentication request

peap_mschapv2_failure.title: PEAP-MSCHAPv2 authentication failure
peap_mschapv2_failure.description: Troubleshoots PEAP-MSCHAPv2 authentication failures involving username/password authentication. Covers password expiration, server certificate validation, NPS configuration, and user account issues.

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=5633)]]" -MaxEvents 5 | Format-List Message
steps.expect: Event 5633 shows PEAP-MSCHAPv2 specific error (often password or server cert related)

steps.action: Get-ADUser <username> -Properties PasswordExpired,PasswordLastSet | Select PasswordExpired,PasswordLastSet
steps.expect: Password is not expired and account is enabled

steps.action: netsh lan show profile name="<profile>"
steps.expect: Profile configured for PEAP with MSCHAPv2 as inner method

steps.action: Get-ChildItem -Path Cert:\LocalMachine\Root | Where Subject -like "*<NPS server cert issuer>*"
steps.expect: NPS/RADIUS server certificate issuing CA is in trusted root store

steps.action: On NPS server: Check NPS server certificate validity and chain
steps.expect: NPS server certificate is valid, trusted, and has Server Authentication EKU

steps.action: Get-WinEvent -LogName Security -FilterXPath "*[System[(EventID=6273)]]" -MaxEvents 10 on NPS server
steps.expect: Reason Code indicates specific failure (23=wrong password, etc.)

steps.action: Test user credentials: Test login to domain with same credentials
steps.expect: User can successfully authenticate to AD domain

steps.action: If password expired: User must change password (Set-ADUser -ChangePasswordAtLogon $true)
steps.expect: User can change password and new password works

steps.action: If server cert not trusted: Add issuing CA to client's trusted root store
steps.expect: NPS server certificate now validates on client

steps.action: If account locked: Unlock account (Unlock-ADAccount <username>)
steps.expect: Account unlocked and can authenticate

steps.action: Temporarily disable server cert validation for testing (not production): In wired profile, uncheck 'Validate server certificate'
steps.expect: If auth succeeds with validation disabled, focus on server certificate trust chain

steps.action: Re-authenticate: disable/enable Ethernet adapter
steps.expect: PEAP-MSCHAPv2 authentication succeeds

steps.action: On switch: show authentication sessions interface <port>
steps.expect: Auth state: Authorized, method shows PEAP

steps.action: On NPS: Check recent authentication events for success
steps.expect: NPS logs show successful authentication for the user

switch_port_config.title: Switch port 802.1x configuration issues
switch_port_config.description: Addresses switch-side configuration problems that prevent 802.1x authentication. Covers port control settings, host mode configuration, authentication order, timer settings, and RADIUS server configuration.

steps.action: On switch: show running-config interface <port> | include dot1x,authentication
steps.expect: 802.1x is enabled and configured on the port

steps.action: On switch: show dot1x interface <port>
steps.expect: Dot1x is operational and shows port status

steps.action: On switch: show authentication sessions interface <port>
steps.expect: Shows authentication state and any error conditions

steps.action: On switch: show running-config interface <port> | include port-control

mab_fallback_failure.title: MAC Authentication Bypass (MAB) fallback not working
mab_fallback_failure.description: Troubleshoots MAB failures for non-802.1x capable devices like printers, IP phones, and legacy equipment. Covers MAC address database configuration, fallback VLAN assignment, and authentication order issues.

steps.action: On switch: show authentication sessions interface <port>
steps.expect: Shows authentication state — may be stuck or failed for MAB

steps.action: On switch: show mac address-table interface <port>
steps.expect: Shows MAC address of the device attempting MAB

steps.action: Check device capabilities: Confirm device does not support 802.1x
steps.expect: Device confirmed as non-802.1x capable

steps.action: On switch: show running-config interface <port> | include authentication event no-response
steps.expect: MAB fallback action is configured (e.g., authorize vlan <restricted VLAN>)

steps.action: On NPS: Check if MAC address is configured as RADIUS client or in user database
steps.expect: MAC address exists in authentication database (format varies by implementation)

steps.action: On switch: Verify authentication order: show running-config | include authentication order
steps.expect: Order allows MAB after 802.1x timeout (dot1x mab or similar)

steps.action: On switch: Check MAB timers: show running-config | include mab timeout
steps.expect: MAB timers are configured appropriately

steps.action: If MAC not in database: Add MAC address to NPS RADIUS clients or user database
steps.expect: MAC address now exists in authentication system

steps.action: If fallback action missing: Configure 'authentication event no-response action authorize vlan <VLAN>'
steps.expect: Fallback VLAN configured for unauthorized devices

steps.action: If authentication order wrong: Set correct order (dot1x before mab for 802.1x-capable devices)
steps.expect: Authentication order allows proper fallback sequence

steps.action: If timers too short: Increase MAB timeout values
steps.expect: MAB has sufficient time to complete

steps.action: On switch: show authentication sessions interface <port>
steps.expect: Shows authorized state via MAB method

steps.action: Verify device in correct VLAN: show interface <port> switchport
steps.expect: Port is in the MAB fallback VLAN

steps.action: Test device connectivity: Ping from device to gateway
steps.expect: Device has network connectivity in restricted VLAN
